newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major accuses Labour of smear politics.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major accuses Labour of smear politics.

text.p: John Major said on Thursday he had not yet talked to the latest Conservative member of parliament to be dogged by damaging pre-election sleaze allegations and accused the main opposition Labour party of smear politics.
The prime minister, asked about allegations that MP Piers Merchant had an affair with a teenage club hostess, said:

"I think Piers Merchant will want to explain the stories in this morning's press to his constituents and others, and as in other cases we need to find out what exactly has happened. I don't yet know that."
Asked if the MP should resign, Major told reporters: "I have seen the newspaper reports, I haven't spoken to Piers Merchant."

Major denied that Wednesday's resignation of former Conservative minister Tim Smith over his failure to declare payments for asking parliamentary questions should prompt other party members facing sleaze allegations to follow suit.
"The other members of parliament of course deny very vigorously any wrongdoing whatsoever," Major said in Bury, a village in his Huntingdon constituency north of London.
Major, facing an uphill struggle to win re-election on May 1, said he did not want to "sweep aside" the raft of allegations, which must all be investigated.
"These allegations are disrupting and of course our political opponents will try and play up whatever allegations appear," he said.
"They (the Labour Party) have a smear a day to keep policies away," the prime minister added.
